deck.caption:
An elderly woman in Telangana recently lost Rs 2.60 lakh in a dry fruits delivery cyber scam, highlighting how easily digital payments and quick online orders can be exploited by fraudsters.

• Understand how a simple delivery text or link leads to financial loss
• Learn why urgent payment requests for small parcels are major warning signs
• Check your own family's digital safety habits before clicking unknown links

Save this post to protect your elders from delivery frauds, and share it with your family group today.

Have you or someone in your home ever received a suspicious payment link for a package you didn't order?

#CyberSafety #FinancialFraud #OnlineScams #SmartInvesting #MarketDebunk

slides.body: A recent report by Telangana Today highlights a harsh reality: an elderly woman lost Rs 2.60 lakh in a dry fruits delivery cyber scam.

slides.title: How the Trap Begins
slides.body: Scammers often send unexpected text messages about a pending parcel or dry fruits delivery, tricking victims into clicking a harmful link or paying a small fee.
slides.card_text: card_text Scammers often send unexpected text messages about a pending parcel or dry fruits delivery, tricking victims into clicking a harmful link or paying a small fee.

slides.title: The Scam Pathway
slides.body:
1. Fake SMS alert received about a delivery
2. Victim clicks an unverified link
3. Fraudsters gain remote access or payment details
4. Life savings drained instantly

slides.title: Expectation vs. Reality
slides.body: Reality: Delivery scams exploit trust and urgency, whereas legitimate couriers never ask for online payments via unknown third-party APK files or random links.
